Q: Why is Chrome sending sec-ch-ua and sec-ch-ua-mobile request headers although "Experimental Web Platform features" are disabled A:

I couldn't find a list of features behind the "Experimental Platform Features" flag, but I assume it's more about experimental Chrome features than experimental web standards, so that this flag probably was never intended to disable client hints, the maturity or stability of the standard behind it notwithstanding. Experimental standards get implemented all the time with current browsers, since that's the only way to get web developers' feedback on the practical implications of the standard.

According to Chrome's Platform Status, client hints are enabled by default since Chrome 89 and seems to be a pre-requisite for the bigger issue of User-Agent string reduction, which is probably one of the reasons it has been implemented quickly.

Q: How to sort a heatmap to show highest correlations together? A:

IIRC, you need to try below, given:

  • heatmap_sorted: sorts by total activity, placing the most active customers and reports in the top-left corner.
  • I used cmap="gray_r" due to lots of '0' as you mentioned to indicates better if no activities
  • Note: since DataFrame contains non-numeric data, we can not use directly df.corr()
  • you may just sort on column if you want:
# Sort heatmap columns by total usage
report_order = heatmap_data.sum(axis=0).sort_values(ascending=False).index
heatmap_sorted_columns = heatmap_data[report_order]

# Pivot table for heatmap (Converts it to a pivot table -- Customer × Report)
heatmap_data = pd.pivot_table(df, values='Count', index='Customer', columns='Report', aggfunc='sum').fillna(0)

# Heatmap: Sort by total usage (simple sorting)
row_order = heatmap_data.sum(axis=1).sort_values(ascending=False).index
col_order = heatmap_data.sum(axis=0).sort_values(ascending=False).index
heatmap_sorted = heatmap_data.loc[row_order, col_order]

#plt.figure(figsize=(18, 14))
#sns.heatmap(np.log1p(heatmap_sorted), cmap="gray_r", vmin=0, vmax=np.log1p(500))
sns.heatmap(heatmap_sorted,           cmap="gray_r", vmin=0)
vmin = heatmap_sorted.values.min()
vmax = heatmap_sorted.values.max()

print(f"Minimum heatmap value: {vmin:.2f}")
print(f"Maximum heatmap value: {vmax:.2f}")
#Minimum heatmap value: 0.00
#Maximum heatmap value: 288.00
